html:
French Guiana is a part of France on the northeast coast of South America, between Suriname and Brazil. Its capital is Cayenne, the name of the old colony on earlier maps. Almost all of it is rainforest.

France held this coast from the 1600s, with sugar and other plantations worked by Africans brought through the Atlantic slave trade. Slavery ended for good in 1848.

In the years shown on the map from 1880, the colony was best known as a prison:

  • From 1852 France shipped convicts here to the bagne, the penal colony, where many died of disease and hard labour.
  • Devil's Island held political prisoners, most famously Alfred Dreyfus from 1895 to 1899.
  • The last convicts went home in the 1950s.

Gold was found in the interior in the late 1800s. Brazil and France both claimed the land to the south, and a Swiss arbitration in 1900 gave most of it to Brazil.

In 1946 French Guiana became an overseas department of France, so it is part of the European Union and uses the euro. Since 1968 the Guiana Space Centre at Kourou, close to the equator, has launched European rockets. Its people include Creoles, descendants of Maroons, Amerindians, Hmong refugees who settled here in the 1970s, and many newcomers from Brazil, Suriname and Haiti.
